summary: Intermittent artifact downloads: DNS falls back to TCP and TLS-inspection blocks resolver TLS, causing model pull failures in private VPC
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent failures downloading model artifacts from our artifact service when running a Private deployment behind their corporate firewall and TGW. Failures correlate with DNS responses that exceed UDP size and trigger TCP fallback; those TCP or TLS-based resolver connections are being intercepted/terminated by the customer's TLS inspection appliance causing name resolution to fail for some requests.

Impact:
- FinSight observed ~15% of artifact download attempts fail in us-east during deployment bumps; streaming generation falling back to smaller cached variants if artifact pull fails.
- Customer-facing inference degraded during autoscale events that trigger new model pulls.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) attached to Transit Gateway.
- Egress through customer perimeter firewall performing TLS inspection (in-line).
- Route53 Resolver outbound endpoint used for split-horizon resolution to internal artifact endpoints.
- Region: us-east.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Trigger a new node scale-up on a private pool to force model artifact download.
2) Observe artifact fetch logs; intermittent DNS failures from the node initiating downstream TCP or DoT to resolver.
3) When resolution fails, HTTP model fetch returns 5xx or times out in the serving-runtime.

Observed behaviour:
- Large DNS responses (AD + DNSSEC / EDNS0) cause UDP truncation -> client retries over TCP or the resolver falls back to DNS-over-TLS (DoT).
- Customer firewall's TLS inspection terminates TLS to resolver IPs and presents a proxy certificate; the resolver rejects the proxied TLS session (SNI mismatch / client cert validation fails) and connection is dropped.
- Result: intermittent NXDOMAIN or timeout for critical artifact hostnames, leading to partial fetch failures.

Expected behaviour:
- DNS TCP fallback and DoT should succeed to the configured resolver endpoint, allowing artifact hostnames to resolve and downloads to proceed.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Packet captures from customer node showing UDP truncation and subsequent TCP/DoT attempt (attachment: finnode1_dns_pcap.pcap).
- Firewall logs showing TLS interception events for resolver IPs (attachment: perimeter_tls_logs-2026-03-01.log).
- Serving-runtime fetch logs showing artifact 504/502 during the same time window.

Temporary workarounds suggested to customer:
- Allow TCP/53 egress to resolver IPs and disable TLS inspection for resolver IPs (or enable TLS passthrough) as a short-term mitigation.
- Reduce EDNS buffer size on resolver/clients (not ideal) to avoid TCP fallback.

Next steps we took:
- Eng and SRE requested packet capture and firewall logs (received 2026-03-01 17:10 UTC).
- SRE reproduced behavior in a staging mirror with an inline TLS proxy configured to terminate DoT.

Resolution (summary):
- Customer allowed TCP/53 and configured an exception on the perimeter TLS inspection appliance for the Route53 resolver IPs used by their VPC endpoints, enabling TLS passthrough to the resolver.
- We also shipped a small client-side change to the agent that lowers EDNS0 buffer preference (config flag) for customers behind appliances that can't be reconfigured; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821.
- After firewall exception and agent config update, FinSight reported artifact fetch success rate returned to baseline (~>99%).

Follow-ups / recommendations:
- Add a KB article for Private deploy customers describing DNS TCP/DoT pitfalls and recommended firewall rules (confluence page created).
- Add a console health check to detect persistent UDP truncation and surface actionable guidance to customers.

investigation_notes:
- Packet capture analysis: client DNS request via UDP received response with TC=1 (truncated) leading to TCP retry.
- TCP sessions attempted to resolver IPs on 53 and to configured DoT endpoint on 853. Both TCP and 853 sessions were intercepted by perimeter TLS proxy which presented a locally-signed cert, causing validation failure.
- Firewall logs: appliance performed MITM on outbound 853 and 443; connection resets observed when server certificate expectations did not match.
- Reproduced in staging by placing an explicit TLS-terminating proxy inline; artifact fetch failures matched production symptoms.
- Confirmed that allowing TCP/53 and configuring TLS passthrough for resolver IPs resolves failures.
- Edge case: some older resolvers still attempt TCP/53 which requires firewall allowlist; recommend customers ensure both TCP/53 and passthrough for 853 if DoT is used.
resolution:
- Customer configured firewall to allow TCP/53 and added an exception to bypass TLS-inspection for Route53 resolver IPs used by their VPC outbound endpoints.
- We merged infra PR to expose an opt-in agent flag for lowering EDNS buffer size as a mitigation for environments that cannot change appliance settings.
- Created KB and updated runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/private-deploy-dns-troubleshooting
- Recommended long-term: customers use resolver endpoints that support UDP-only answers or configure perimeter devices for TLS passthrough to resolvers.
